correctness.rationale: The proof uses exact double counting of one-edge extensions of consecutive forest levels. A line-graph path bound and a cycle union bound give an average complete-graph extension deficit below one for n >= 3k^2. The k=3 boundary case is completed for every admissible n by an exact deficit formula, edge-transitivity, and finite inclusion-exclusion for the two remaining complement types.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The motivating arXiv:2609.18611 states the full consecutive-ratio inequality as Conjecture 5.8 but does not give the square-root boundary layer or the all-order k=3 case. Exact and synonymous searches found no prior equivalent statement. The conjecture is extremely recent, so unindexed parallel work remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The result proves a growing O(sqrt(n))-width family of levels of a new stronger spanning-forest conjecture and completely settles the first nontrivial fixed boundary rank where cycle corrections enter.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
